summary: Enhance team cohesion, improve productivity, and foster a positive work environment by building high-trust teams with our comprehensive training course.
lede: Building trust in teams means diagnosing trust patterns and shaping the behaviors that support safe, reliable collaboration. For professionals who lead, coordinate, or support teams, the course develops practical ways to assess trust, encourage psychological safety, and establish clear team agreements. It also covers trust-preserving feedback and conflict conversations, repairing broken commitments, and using simple measures and routines to sustain trust.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who lead, coordinate, or support teams and need practical ways to strengthen trust while still delivering results. If you manage people, facilitate collaboration, or handle the consequences of low trust in projects or operations, this program gives you concrete tools to use immediately with your teams. This course is designed for: Team Leaders responsible for day-to-day coordination and team delivery outcomes. Project Managers overseeing cross-functional project teams and stakeholder commitments. Scrum Masters guiding agile teams and protecting psychological safety in ceremonies. HR Business Partners supporting managers with trust, conflict, and engagement issues. People Managers supervising an intact team and handling performance conversations. Operations Supervisors coordinating frontline teams under time and quality pressures. Product Owners aligning cross-functional squads around shared backlog priorities. Functional Leads managing specialists who must collaborate across disciplines. Change Managers facilitating trust during restructures, new processes, or system rollout. Learning and Development Specialists designing programs to strengthen team trust behaviors.
modules: Interpersonal Trust: Sincerity, Reliability, Competence, Care
High-Trust Communication, Feedback, and Conflict Handling
Repairing Broken Trust and Rebuilding Relationships
Trust in Cross-Functional, Remote, and Diverse Teams
Sustaining High-Trust Teams: Metrics, Rituals, and Roadmap
prerequisites: You should currently work with or manage a team so you can apply the tools and frameworks to live situations. Basic familiarity with day-to-day team operations, meetings, and performance expectations is assumed. Bring examples of recent conflicts, misaligned commitments, or engagement challenges you want to work through. A laptop or device with access to standard office and collaboration tools is recommended for working with digital templates and simple pulse survey examples.
